Augu{{ls}}tine, ''Fidei {{ls}}implicitate & {{ls}}inceritate lactati, nutriamur in Chri{{ls}}to: & cum parui {{ls}}umus, maiorum cibos non appetamus.'' that is, ''Being fed vvith the {{ls}}implicitie and {{ls}}inceritie of faith, as it vvere vvith milke, {{ls}}o let'' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''De bono per{{ls}}euer. c. 16.''}}''vs be nouri{{ls}}hed in Chri{{ls}}t: and vvhen vve are litle ones, let vs not couet the meates of the elder {{ls}}ort.'' Vvho in an other place te{{ls}}tifieth, that the vvord of God can not be preached nor certaine my{{ls}}teries vttered to all men alike, but are to be {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1 Cor. 3.''}}deliuered according to the capacitie of the hearers: as he proueth both by S. Paules example, vvho gaue not to euery {{ls}}ort {{ls}}trong meate, but milke to many, as being {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 16.''}}not {{ls}}piritual, but carnal and not capable: and by our lordes al{{ls}}o, vvho {{ls}}pake to {{ls}}ome plainely, and to others in parables, & affirmed that he had many things to vtter vvhich the hearers vvere not able to beare.

Hovv much more may vve gather, that all thinges that be vvritten, are not for the capacitie and diet of euery of the {{ls}}imple readers, but that very many my{{ls}}teries of holy vvritte, be very far aboue their reach, & may and ought to be (by as great rea{{ls}}on) deliuered them in mea{{ls}}ure & meane mo{{ls}}t meete for them? {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''In orat. de modera. in di{{ls}}p. {{ls}}erua. in fine. Hiero. in proœm. cōmentar. in Ezechi.''}}vvhich in deede can hardly be done, vvhen the vvhole booke of the Bible {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Ievves lavv for not reading certaine bookes of holy Scripture vntil a time.}}lieth before euery man in his mother tonge, to make choi{{ls}}e of vvhat he li{{ls}}t. For vvhich cau{{ls}}e the {{ls}}aid Gregorie Nazianzen vvi{{ls}}heth the Chri{{ls}}tians had as good a lavv as the Hebrues of old had: vvho (as S. Hierom al{{ls}}o vvitne{{ls}}{{ls}}eth) tooke order among them {{ls}}elues that none {{ls}}hould read the ''Cantica Canticorum'' nor certaine other pieces of harde{{ls}}t Scriptures, till they vvere thirtie yeres of age.

And truely there is no cau{{ls}}e vvhy men {{ls}}hould be more loth to be ordered and moderated in this point by Gods Church and their Pa{{ls}}tors, then they are in the v{{ls}}e of holy Sacraments: for vvhich as Chri{{ls}}t hath appointed Prie{{ls}}tes and mini{{ls}}ters, at vvho{{ls}}e handes vve mu{{ls}}t receiue them, and not be our owne caruers: {{ls}}o hath he giuen {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Eph. 4.''}} vs doctors, prophetes, expoūders, interpreters, teachers and preachers, to take the lavv and our faith at their mouthes: becau{{ls}}e our faith and religion commeth not to vs properly or principally by reading of {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ro. 10, 17.''}}Scriptures, but (as the Apo{{ls}}tle {{ls}}aith) by hearing of the preachers lavvfully {{ls}}ent: though reading in order and humilitie, much confirmeth and aduanceth the {{ls}}ame. Therfore this holy booke of the Scriptures, is called of S. Ambro{{ls}}e, ''Liber {{ls}}acerdotalis, the booke of prie{{ls}}tes,'' at vvho{{ls}}e handes and di{{ls}}po{{ls}}ition vve mu{{ls}}t take and v{{ls}}e it. ''Li. 2. ad Grat.''

{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The popular obiections of vvithholding the Scriptures from the people, an{{ls}}vvered.}}The vvi{{ls}}e vvil not here regard vvhat {{ls}}ome vvilful people do mutter, that the Scriptures are made for all men, and that it is of enuie that the Prie{{ls}}tes do keepe the holy booke from them. Vvhich {{ls}}ugge{{ls}}tion commeth of the {{ls}}ame {{ls}}erpent {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 3.''}} that {{ls}}educed our fir{{ls}}t parents, vvho per{{ls}}uaded them, that God had forbidden them that tree of knovvledge, le{{ls}}t they {{ls}}hould be as cunning as him{{ls}}elf, and like vnto the Highe{{ls}}t. No, no, the church doth it to keepe them from {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Vvhy the Church permitteth not euery one at their plea{{ls}}ure to reade the Scripture.}}blind ignorant pre{{ls}}umption, and from that vvhich the Apo{{ls}}tle calleth ''fal{{ls}}i nominis {{ls}}cientiam knovvledge fal{{ls}}ely {{ls}}o called:''{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1 Tim. 6, 20.''}} and not to embarre them from the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ro. 12, 3.''}}true knovvledge, of Chri{{ls}}t. She vvould haue all vvi{{ls}}e, but ''v{{ls}}que ad {{ls}}obrietatem, vnto {{ls}}obrietie,'' as the Apo{{ls}}tle {{ls}}peaketh: {{ls}}he knovveth the Scriptures be ordained for euery {{ls}}tate, as meates, elements, fire, vvater, candle, kniues, {{ls}}vvord, & the like:<noinclude>{{continues|vvhich}}</noinclude>
